question: Compare covariance and correlation.
answer: Covariance measures the direction and strength of a linear relationship between two variables, unlike correlation which ranges from -1 to +1, indicating strength and direction, but does not imply causation [S6] [S7].

citations.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
citations.text: 6. Correlation and Regression Correlation measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables. The Pearson correlation coefficient r ranges from -1 to +1. A value near +1 indicates a strong positive linear relationship, near -1 a strong negative one and near 0 no linear relationship. Correlation does not imply causation: a hidden confounding variable may drive both variables. Simple linear regression fits the line y-hat = b0 + b1 * x by least squares, which minimizes the sum of squared residuals. The slope b1 equals r * (s_y / s_x) and the intercept is b0 = y-bar - b1 * x-bar. The coefficient of determination R squared is the proportion of variance in y explained by the model; in simple regression it equals r squared. Residual plots should show no pattern; curved or funnel-shaped residuals indicate a violated assumption.

S1.title: Statistics Confusable Terms
S1.text: standard deviation vs standard error: the standard deviation describes the spread of individual observations; the standard error describes the spread of a statistic such as the sample mean across repeated samples. confidence level vs confidence interval: the level (for example 95%) is a property of the procedure; the interval is the computed range of values. significance level vs p-value: alpha is chosen before the test; the p-value is computed from the data. covariance vs correlation: covariance carries the units of x times the units of y; correlation is unitless and always between -1 and 1. precision of a measurement: how close repeated measurements are to each other. Precision in classification is a different concept (see the machine learning course). normal: the normal distribution is the bell curve. It does not mean "typical" or "healthy" values.

S3.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S3.text:
2. Variance in Machine Learning
In machine learning the variance of a model is how much its predictions change when it is trained
on different training sets drawn from the same source. High-variance models such as deep
decision trees fit the quirks of one training set. This is a property of the learning algorithm, not the
spread of a data column.
The spread of a feature column is a different matter. In scikit-learn VarianceThreshold removes
features whose variance is below a threshold; the default threshold is 0.0, which removes only
constant features.

S4.title: Statistics Lab Report Guide
S4.text:
Anscombe's Quartet
Anscombe's quartet consists of four small datasets that have almost identical means, variances and correlation (about 0.816) but completely different shapes when plotted. The lesson is to always plot the data and not to rely on summary statistics alone.

S5.title: Statistics Estimators And Bias
S5.text:
2. Variance of an Estimator
The variance of an estimator describes how much the estimate changes from one random sample
to the next. For the sample mean it equals sigma squared divided by n, so the standard error of the
mean is sigma divided by the square root of n.
This is not the same quantity as the variance of the data themselves, which describes the spread
of individual observations around their mean. Quadrupling the sample size halves the standard
error but does not change the variance of the data.
